description: Whether Google considers the property safe to send people to. These are the failures that remove a site from results wholesale rather than costing it positions: a Safe Browsing flag, a manual action, a broken certificate, a page served differently to a crawler than to a visitor. Nothing in the repository proves any of them, because every one is a judgement Google makes about the live host and the company it keeps.

gates.title: Safe Browsing Reports The Site Clean
gates.rule: The Safe Browsing service returns no threat match for the domain or any subdomain. A match puts a full-page interstitial in front of every visitor arriving from search or Chrome, and traffic goes to zero the same day.
gates.fix: Query the Safe Browsing Lookup API for the host and its subdomains. If a threat is listed, find and remove the flagged resource, then request a review in the Search Console security issues report.

gates.title: Every URL Serves Over HTTPS With A Valid Chain
gates.rule: The canonical host serves HTTPS with a certificate that matches the name, is inside its validity window, and presents its full intermediate chain. A chain that validates in a browser holding a cached intermediate still fails for a crawler that holds none.
gates.fix: Serve the intermediates alongside the leaf, correct the name on the certificate where it excludes the apex or the www host, and reissue before expiry.

gates.title: The Certificate Renews Ahead Of Expiry
gates.rule: The certificate has more than 30 days of validity left and renews without a hand on it. An expired certificate is an unclickable browser warning, and it lands on a weekend as often as not.
gates.fix: Confirm automatic renewal is running at the host or CDN, and read the current expiry rather than trusting that renewal is configured.

gates.title: No Page Loads A Resource Over Plain HTTP
gates.rule: No document loads a script, stylesheet, image, font or frame over HTTP. Mixed content is blocked or downgraded by the browser, so the page a visitor sees is not the page that was tested.
gates.fix: Fetch each template and list the HTTP subresources, then correct the URLs in the repository through seo-checklist or the owning project.

gates.title: No Manual Action Stands Against The Property
gates.rule: The manual actions report is empty. A manual action is a human decision at Google to demote or remove the site, and it persists until a reconsideration request is filed and accepted, however clean the site becomes.
gates.fix: Read the manual actions report through the Search Console API, remove what the action names, then file a reconsideration request describing what was removed and how it happened.

gates.title: No Security Issue Is Open In Search Console
gates.rule: The security issues report shows no hacked content, malware, social engineering or unwanted software finding. These are reported separately from manual actions and carry their own review cycle.
gates.fix: Read the security issues report, clean the URLs it names, close the entry point that allowed the injection, then request a review.

gates.title: No Hacked Or Injected Content Is Served
gates.rule: No page serves spam text, hidden links, injected redirects or content in a language the site does not publish in. Injected content is served selectively, so a page that looks clean to the owner can be spam to a crawler or to a visitor arriving from search.
gates.fix: Fetch the site with a search crawler user agent and with a search referrer, compare against a plain fetch, and remove what only appears in one of them.

gates.title: Googlebot Receives The Page A Visitor Receives
gates.rule: The response to a crawler and the response to a browser carry the same content. Serving a different page by user agent is cloaking whether it was meant as one or fell out of a caching layer, and it is enforced as a policy breach either way.
gates.fix: Fetch each template as Googlebot and as a normal browser and compare the rendered text. Where a CDN or bot-protection rule causes the difference, allow the verified crawler through it.

gates.title: The Inbound Link Profile Is One Nobody Paid For
gates.rule: The links report holds no pattern of paid, exchanged or automated inbound links. Link schemes are the most common cause of a manual action, and a site inherits the ones a previous owner or a previous agency bought.
gates.fix: Export the top linking sites from the Search Console links report and read the pattern. Where paid links cannot be removed at the source, file a disavow for those domains.

gates.title: Every Third-Party Script Is One That Will Not Flag The Domain
gates.rule: Each third-party script embedded on the site is served from a host the owner recognises and would defend. A widget, a chat box or an ad tag pulling further scripts at runtime puts the domain's reputation in someone else's release process.
gates.fix: List the third-party origins each page loads, remove what nobody can name an owner for, and pin the rest to a versioned URL with subresource integrity where the vendor supports it.
